Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Reported fixed proverb clause; numeral + plural nominal subject followed by object and finite verb, closed by quotative/evidential wone.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Lazy or like-minded people tend to pair together; also a warning that difficult work demands devotion, not idle companionship.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Lazy people often associate with each other, and hard work requires serious effort.
Usage Contexts: agriculture; family advice; humor; criticism of laziness; peer influence
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Field-recorded Kafa proverb tied to teff cultivation, where careful tilling, fencing, and weeding are required; source: https://academicjournals.org/article/article1408008915_Dagnew%20and%20Wodajo.pdf
First Example Sentence: Gaashoo gogaheesin kashoo qoodde; Gutta yeexaroo gaashoo gogahe wone.
Second Example Sentence: Yeexaroo shoochchi shoochchi beete; Gutta yeexaroo gaashoo gogahe wone.
Third Example Sentence: Bonga gabiyoon kaashii naaton naato wone: Gutta yeexaroo gaashoo gogahe wone.

Idiom (Kafa): Ashi gattoo gibanaaye ne kootaroo battaaye.
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Bipartite imperative/admonitory clause; dependent temporal phrase plus negative imperative with second-person possessive object.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Do not depend entirely on someone else’s resources; start with what you have before the right season or chance passes.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Be self-reliant and act with your own means while waiting for help.
Usage Contexts: farming; entrepreneurship; schoolwork; workplace planning; youth advice
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Recorded in a farming context where poor farmers wait for borrowed oxen but must not miss the cultivation season; source: https://academicjournals.org/article/article1408008915_Dagnew%20and%20Wodajo.pdf
First Example Sentence: Ashi gattoo gibanaaye ne kootaroo battaaye; gochii yooyoon qitiyo.
Second Example Sentence: Ne ashi qooddee qoppite, kootaroo battaaye, wone maacoo.
Third Example Sentence: Qawoon woyiteenna, ashi gattoo gibanaaye ne kootaroo battaaye.

Idiom (Kafa): Gochii nattitoyee gabii nattito mechee tunabana.
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Comparative proverb clause; future-oriented planning phrase contrasted with completed-action cultivation phrase.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Careful planning is worth more than hasty present action; preparation produces better results than unsystematic work.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Planning ahead is better than acting without a plan.
Usage Contexts: agriculture; household management; leadership; project planning; gentle criticism
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Collected from a Kafa household-agricultural context criticizing messy planting and weak field fencing; source: https://academicjournals.org/article/article1408008915_Dagnew%20and%20Wodajo.pdf
First Example Sentence: Gochii nattitoyee gabii nattito mechee tunabana; shuutii qawoon qooda.
Second Example Sentence: Gojjebon eeggeena wode, gochii nattitoyee gabii nattito mechee tunabana.
Third Example Sentence: Kafachoch gishshoon kaallo qoodde: Gochii nattitoyee gabii nattito mechee tunabana.

Idiom (Kafa): Shaacee ginee koyoyee ash ginee koyo gaawa.
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Comparative metaphorical clause; nominalized spear-images contrasted by evaluative predicate.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Hunger and neglect can injure a whole household more severely than a visible personal wound.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Failing to provide food and livelihood can harm the whole family.
Usage Contexts: family responsibility; famine warnings; conflict mediation; elders’ counsel; moral teaching
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Rooted in Kafa fears of hunger and the importance of crops, especially false banana, for household survival; source: https://academicjournals.org/article/article1408008915_Dagnew%20and%20Wodajo.pdf
Phonetic Transcription (IPA, Kafa): [ʃaːtʃeː ɡineː kojojeː aʃ ɡineː kojo ɡaːwa]
First Example Sentence: Shaacee ginee koyoyee ash ginee koyo gaawa, wone ebiitoch.
Second Example Sentence: Maaloo qixxeena ashich shaacee ginee koyoyee ash ginee koyo gaawa.
Third Example Sentence: Woyina gochii fooni baate, shaacee ginee koyoyee ash ginee koyo gaawa.

Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Negative existential proverb; conditional/privative forest phrase plus ethnic dative/benefactive noun phrase.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: The forest is essential to Kafa life; destroying it threatens material, cultural, and spiritual survival.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Kafa people need forests for their way of life and must protect them.
Usage Contexts: environment; public meetings; land use; spirituality; cultural education
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Connected to Kafa forest-based agriculture, forest coffee, honey, construction materials, medicine, and sacred Eqqo/Deejjo sites; source: https://academicjournals.org/article/article1408008915_Dagnew%20and%20Wodajo.pdf
First Example Sentence: Kubbo aallegaata Kafachoch kashoo aalle; kubbo qooddeena beete.

Third Example Sentence: Kasho qixxeena gishshoon kubbo aallegaata Kafachoch kashoo aalle.

Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Nominalized path metaphor plus negative-result clause; compact moral maxim.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Doing things the right and lawful way prevents shame and social blame.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Follow the proper path so you do not bring disgrace.
Usage Contexts: law; trade; family reputation; public advice; ethical correction
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Explained through rural road/fence disputes and also used in advice about legal coffee trade; source: https://academicjournals.org/article/article1408008915_Dagnew%20and%20Wodajo.pdf

Idiom (Kafa): Ne heciyo qitiba ne bushoo qitiba getee ta bushoo qitba iye wone.
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Reported comparative proverb; second-person possessive nouns contrasted through loss/valuation predicate and quotative closure.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Truthfulness and keeping one’s word are more valuable than almost anything, even deeply cherished family ties.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Keep your promise and protect your reputation for truth.
Usage Contexts: oaths; mediation; family honor; agreements; leadership ethics
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Represents the high Kafa social value placed on one’s tongue/word as a symbol of promise, loyalty, and truth; source: https://academicjournals.org/article/article1408008915_Dagnew%20and%20Wodajo.pdf
Phonetic Transcription (IPA, Kafa): [ne hetʃijo qitiba ne buʃoː qitiba ɡeteː ta buʃoː qitba ije wone]

Second Example Sentence: Qitba qooddeena ashoon ne heciyo qitiba ne bushoo qitiba getee ta bushoo qitba iye wone.
Third Example Sentence: Maacoo naaton wone: Ne heciyo qitiba ne bushoo qitiba getee ta bushoo qitba iye wone.

Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Contrastive imperative proverb; elder-by-birth phrase negated/contrasted with elder-in-wisdom object.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Seek counsel from wisdom, not merely from age; experience and insight matter more than seniority alone.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Ask the wise person, not just the oldest person.
Usage Contexts: counsel; education; dispute settlement; family decision-making; mentorship
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Reflects Kafa ideas that elders are respected, but wisdom is not guaranteed by age alone; source: https://academicjournals.org/article/article1408008915_Dagnew%20and%20Wodajo.pdf
First Example Sentence: Shiijji qaabboyee ariiya qaabbon echabi, wone deejjecho.

Third Example Sentence: Gommoon baqqeena, shiijji qaabboyee ariiya qaabbon echabi.

Idiom (Kafa): Qappi ariiyaanooch qamoo shaawushoone iye wone.
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Metaphorical nominal clause with experiencer dative; soft-organ noun equated to hard-bone predicate; quotative closure.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: For someone without experience, even an easy task feels difficult.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Inexperience makes simple work seem hard.
Usage Contexts: skill learning; work training; riding; cooking; craftsmanship; humorous correction
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Draws on Kafa raw-meat preparation, where skilled cutters easily cut liver while inexperienced people struggle; source: https://academicjournals.org/article/article1408008915_Dagnew%20and%20Wodajo.pdf
First Example Sentence: Qappi ariiyaanooch qamoo shaawushoone iye wone; ashich qooddiyo.
Second Example Sentence: Fardoon shoodaana qappi ariiyaanooch qamoo shaawushoone iye wone.
Third Example Sentence: Gochii kaxxoon qappi ariiyaanooch qamoo shaawushoone iye wone.

Idiom (Kafa): Mooyo bulli maacooch beetee noona kettoona kechye wone.
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Contrastive proverb clause; universal quantifier subject contrasted with talkative-person agent and verb of disclosure; quotative closure.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Most people keep secrets, but a talkative person exposes what should remain hidden.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Do not trust a talkative person with confidential information.
Usage Contexts: secrecy; friendship; politics; family matters; sarcasm; social criticism
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: From Kafa social norms that value secrecy and criticize excessive talk as socially abnormal or unreliable behavior; source: https://academicjournals.org/article/article1408008915_Dagnew%20and%20Wodajo.pdf
Phonetic Transcription (IPA, Kafa): [moːjo bulːi maːtʃoːtʃ beːteː noːna ketːoːna ketʃje wone]

Second Example Sentence: Noona kettoona woyite, mooyo bulli maacooch beetee noona kettoona kechye wone.
Third Example Sentence: Gabiye gishshoon maacoo wone: Mooyo bulli maacooch beetee noona kettoona kechye wone.
